message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  In total, the combined losses of the French and the Anglo‑Dutch‑Prussian coalition were **around 23 000 men** who were killed, wounded or taken prisoner/missing.

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| French (including allied contingents) | ~25 000 |
| Anglo‑Dutch‑Prussian coalition | ~22 000 |

These figures come from the most widely cited contemporary reports and modern scholarship.  The numbers vary slightly depending on the source, but the consensus places the total casualties in the low‑to‑mid 20,000s.
